The evidence the phase originally filed for it — `wi6-lease-failing.txt`/`wi6-lease-passing.txt`, 2026-07-17 — certified a guarantee the code did not have: `writeExclusive` did `open(path,"wx")` and then a SEPARATE write, so the lease path was briefly observable EMPTY; a contender read `""`, `parseLeaseRecord("")` returned `undefined`, and `isTakeoverEligible(undefined, …)` returns `true` UNCONDITIONALLY (lease-record.ts:104) without ever consulting pid liveness. That was the THIRD distinct cause of the same intermittent failure in this very test (the earlier two: a fixed 300ms hold that let the race not happen at all, fixed 2026-07-30; synthetic pids that made liveness permanently false, fixed in #43/`16fb82f`). RESIDUAL, stated rather than papered over: the `record === undefined` branch of `isTakeoverEligible` still takes over unconditionally, including against a live process — `lease-record.test.ts:96` asserts exactly that ('expect(isTakeoverEligible(undefined, Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, true)).toBe(true);'). It is sound only because, after `70d7da7`, no correct process can leave a present-but-unparseable lease file: publication stages the complete record under a private name and `link()`s it into place. The criterion's "never against a live process" therefore rests on the producer side, not on the eligibility predicate. W4's separate takeover-rename TOCTOU residual (evidence README Deviation 3) also remains open with a sharpened precondition. FLAKE, measured rather than waved at. Two arms of `lease.test.ts` are separately tracked as real-timer races in the tests' OWN choreography: `onLeaseLost` and the `autoRenew` heartbeat-renewal arm. Both passed in the cited CI run at `af46e00` and in this pass's first scoped capture, but `onLeaseLost` then failed 5/5 when `lease.test.ts` was run alone and 3/3 in the six-file form, and once in the full `npm test` (1 failed | 6060 passed). The mechanism is visible in the test: A holds with a 10ms heartbeat, the lease file is unlinked out-of-band, and B re-acquires — if A's heartbeat fires in the window between the unlink and B's publish, A correctly reports `missing` where the test asserts `ownership_mismatch` (`lease.test.ts:579`). It is not this pass's doing (`git diff origin/main -- packages/` is empty here) and it is not attributed to `70d7da7` either — that is speculation this pass did not test. criteria.notes: SENSITIVITY, quantified so the tick is not read as more than it is. Both clauses the criterion names are real — a committed benchmark output, and a gate that this pass confirmed executing in CI from the job log. What the gate will NOT catch is most of what "regression" usually means: the threshold is 100ms against a p50 this pass re-measured at 2.70ms idle, i.e. ~37x headroom, and 13.34ms under heavy concurrent load, i.e. ~7.5x. A 5x append-latency regression passes it silently. The margin is deliberate and documented (`append-benchmark.test.ts:16-25` cites roadmap/04's own §Risks note that "fsync semantics differ on WSL2 9p mounts"; this repo's dev environment is WSL2, and the two captures above differ by 4.9x on one machine within five minutes, which is the variance that reasoning is about). The criterion states no sensitivity requirement, so this is a scope note rather than a defect — but a reader should treat this box as evidencing a catastrophic-regression smoke gate, not a tuned p50 budget. 15's `PerformanceContract`/`perf-conformance` machinery is where a tuned budget would belong.
